html:
Killing of thousands of unarmed people of Cholula, in central Mexico, by the Spanish and their native allies in October 1519.

Hernan Cortes was marching on Tenochtitlan with a few hundred Spaniards and many warriors from Tlaxcala, who hated Cholula as an ally of the Mexica. Cholula was a holy city with the Great Pyramid. The Spanish said they had learned of a plot to attack them, with help from Moctezuma. Their interpreter Malinche is said to have warned Cortes.

The Spanish gathered the Cholulans in a courtyard and attacked. Estimates of the dead run from about 3,000 to 6,000 or more, and the city was looted and burned. Whether a plot existed is still debated, and Cortes may have wanted to terrify the road ahead.

The massacre worked as a warning. Moctezuma let the Spanish enter his capital a few weeks later, in November. Cholula's people then joined the Spanish side against the Mexica.
sum: Killing of thousands of unarmed people of Cholula, in central Mexico, by the Spanish and their native allies in October 1519.
